title: Interest rates and Bank Rate: our latest decision
summary: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 19 March 2026, marking the sixth consecutive hold following six cuts since August 2024. The committee cited the Middle East war as a driver of higher energy prices, which will push inflation above prior expectations in the near term. Current inflation stands at 3% against a 2% target.
key_points: Bank Rate held at 3.75% – unchanged from prior meeting
Six rate cuts have been implemented since August 2024
War in the Middle East has disrupted energy transportation and supply, raising energy prices
Higher energy costs will push up households' fuel and utility prices and increase companies' production costs
Inflation will be higher than expected at least in the short term due to energy price pressures
Current inflation rate is 3%, versus the 2% target
Next MPC meeting scheduled for 30 April 2026
why_it_matters: The Bank of England is signaling that geopolitical energy disruptions are creating upward inflation pressure at a time when monetary policymakers had been normalizing rates. This could complicate the path toward further easing if energy-driven inflation proves persistent, affecting mortgage costs, consumer spending power, and business cost structures across the UK economy.
macro_context: The source explicitly attributes near-term inflation upward pressure to Middle East conflict disrupting global energy supply. Higher energy costs are identified as a potential drag on economic activity as purchasing power is redirected to fuel and utilities. The MPC is assessing these second-order effects on inflation. The source states monetary policy cannot directly affect global energy prices.
notes: Source is from Bank of England's institutional page; authoritative domain. Published 26 days before TODAY, well within the 90-day threshold – considered recent.
